steps.desc: e9patch corpus driver contracts (typed build-info and engagement readers)
steps.description: tests/e9patch/e9patch_corpus.py ratchets e9patch preprocessing parity against golden ptrace, but it needs e9tool and a Hermit built with the e9patch cargo feature, and CI has neither, so no validation lane runs its guests. This node runs tests/e9patch/test_e9patch_corpus.py, which checks the driver without running Hermit or compiling a guest: the build-info reader follows the boolean features.e9patch of a schema-1 `hermit version --json` record and refuses a record without it by field name; the engagement reader follows the producer's candidate, mapped and B0 site counts and refuses a record that lacks one; corpus commands use the caller's private host --tmp root rather than host /tmp; and `e9patch_corpus.py --check` finds exactly the corpus guest sources. The six reader checks ran in check.backend_parity_suites, inside tests/backend-parity/test_verify_tier_evidence.py, until the corpus moved out of tests/backend-parity in slice S13 of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3301. The --tmp check came from tests/backend-parity/test_parallel_validate_paths.py, which no node ran. The same maintained patching owner also runs the nine real-ELF portability controls, both actual produce/verify RUNPATH call-site controls, and the original real-kernel target-basename/Linux-limit task-name control. Original 60-wall/7200-CPU/memory bounds retained; no Cargo/guest/backend build is hidden in these tiny C fixture controls.
steps.cmd: export PATH="$PWD/ci/rust-script-bin:$PATH"; export HERMIT_RUST_SCRIPT_ARTIFACT_ROOT="$PWD/target/ci/rust-scripts"; export HERMIT_PREBUILT_RUST_SCRIPTS_REQUIRED=1; python3 "${HERMIT_PATCHING_ROOT:?}/tests/e9patch/test_e9patch_corpus.py" && python3 -B "${HERMIT_PATCHING_ROOT:?}/hermit-patching-cli/native/test_portable_preload.py" && python3 -B "${HERMIT_PATCHING_ROOT:?}/hermit-patching-cli/native/test_preload_publication.py" && python3 -B "${HERMIT_PATCHING_ROOT:?}/hermit-patching-cli/native/test_guest_comm.py"

steps.desc: The compatibility corpus on SaBRe
steps.description: The sabre-compat-only run type: `test-harness run --label sabre-compat-only` over tests/e2e/manifests/compat.yaml, so it runs exactly the cells labelled with that run type and nothing the full validation runs. Those are each corpus row's SaBRe verify cell (the `focused` section: every row but lsof, netlink-route, netlink-sock-diag and shell-build) and both cells of the 30 rows only this run type has (23 programs the SaBRe corpus had and the strict corpus lacks; lua-direct, perl-direct and df-direct, which keep that corpus's single-image argv for programs whose strict rows run under a bash wrapper; and rustc, javac, java and node, whose ptrace cells get 600 seconds). It runs the validation's one Hermit build, the e2e artifact build.host_hermit_link links on the host, whose install tree carries the SaBRe loader and libdetcore_sabre.so, against the fixtures sabrecompatprep.fixtures writes; each cell runs Hermit's strict --verify (--verify-strict) once and must also pass the harness's SaBRe execution-path contract (an RPC from the in-guest tool, zero ptrace-fallback and zero trusted shared-object system-call sites). A cell measured red stays enabled with `ci: false` and its failure class's issue (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3486 and the issues it names), so `--ci-only` selects only the cells that pass. The guest's own dynamic loader loads libdetcore_sabre.so against the guest's libc, so the artifact's publication and verification refuse a plugin that records a library search path, needs a library outside glibc, or requires a glibc symbol version newer than 2.34 (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3652). A program that diverges, crashes or leaves SaBRe's measured path turns it red. Until 2026-10-01 these rows were 212 separate sabrecompat.<program> nodes that checked only Hermit's exit status, so a program whose children ran outside SaBRe passed, and on a fresh checkout their release Hermit had no SaBRe loader at all. The node's 2120-second wall bound is the 1820 seconds `scripts/validate.rs --self-test` requires of it as outer headroom, plus 300 seconds for the rest of the bucket, so a hung heavy cell is reported as that cell's timeout rather than ending the node. The self-test models every manifest cell as two attempts with 10 seconds of termination grace each, and its representative 1.5x wall multiplier turns the largest selected cells (rustc and node on ptrace, 600 seconds each) into 900-second windows: 2 x (900 + 10). The two attempts are that conservative model only; compat cells carry the manifest's no_retry_reason, so the harness never retries them.
steps.cmd: export PATH="$PWD/ci/rust-script-bin:$PATH"; export HERMIT_RUST_SCRIPT_ARTIFACT_ROOT="$PWD/target/ci/rust-scripts"; export HERMIT_PREBUILT_RUST_SCRIPTS_REQUIRED=1; ./ci/run-with-hermit-e2e-artifact.sh --require-install HERMIT_E2E_COMMAND_BINDINGS="${HERMIT_SABRE_BINDINGS:?}" "${HERMIT_CORE_TOOLS:?}/test-harness" run --execution-owner patching --repo-root "${HERMIT_CORE_SOURCE:?}" --lane portable --category compat --label sabre-compat-only --ci-only --prebuilt --diagnostic-results --results "$E2E_RESULT_ROOT/portable/manifest_compat/results.jsonl" --junit "$E2E_RESULT_ROOT/portable/manifest_compat/junit.xml"

steps.desc: SaBRe smoke test (archived backend): ptrace parity and canonical verify of one guest
steps.description: SaBRe is archived (owner, 2026-10-25: no feature work, tests nightly only; ci/manifest-plan/src/archived.rs), so per commit this node is its smoke test, beside the third-party-backends build and Clippy that keep its code compiling. It runs two tests of hermit-cli/tests/sabre_examples.rs, its count pinned by NEXTEST_EXPECTED_EXECUTED, against an explicitly configured SaBRe loader, so a missing loader, libdetcore_sabre.so or revision file fails rather than skips: sabre_root_pid_matches_ptrace requires a root-PID shell probe to give identical status, stdout and stderr under ptrace and --backend sabre, the SaBRe controller's diagnostics to stay out of guest stderr, and the SaBRe run to pass `--verify --verify-strict` with bitwise_parity true; sabre_and_ptrace_detlogs_agree_through_post_exec requires the DETLOG records the SaBRe plugin forwards for /bin/true to equal ptrace's through the post-exec AT_RANDOM record. steps.desc: Stage the release backend resources for the host e9patch cells
steps.description: Runs `cargo build --release --locked -p detcore-dbt`, then a release build of hermit with third-party-backends together with detcore-dbt, its shared object detcore-dbt-cdylib, detcore-sabre and hermit-install, both through ci/run-with-reverie-dbt-budget.sh (which sets Cargo's job count from the calibrated DBT build budget), then finalizes the ordinary Detcore preload with `target/release/stage-detcore-liteinst --git target` in the existing liteinst-runtime profile and unchanged constructor/source proof, and finally `test -x` on target/install_pkg/rsrcs/e9patch and e9tool. The e9patchcompat probes run the host release Hermit built by compatprep.hermit_release, which finds its packaged resources, the e9patch and e9tool binaries among them, through target/install_pkg; this node stages that tree for the e9patch-compat-only profile. steps.desc: e9patch files-only NSS fixture
steps.description: Writes a files-only nsswitch.conf (every database, aliases through shadow, set to "files") to $VALIDATE_RUN_STATE/e9patchcompat/nsswitch.conf with mkdir and printf. The six probes whoami, groups, pinky, logname, tar and chown bind it read-only over /etc/nsswitch.conf, because they look up user and group names that the host may resolve through an identity daemon; pinning them to files keeps that host race out of the e9patch compatibility measurement. It runs after release_resources, and the lane's fixtures node waits for it. It fails only if the run-state directory cannot be created or written, which shows as a mkdir or printf error.
steps.cmd:
export PATH="$PWD/ci/rust-script-bin:$PATH"; export HERMIT_RUST_SCRIPT_ARTIFACT_ROOT="$PWD/target/ci/rust-scripts"; export HERMIT_PREBUILT_RUST_SCRIPTS_REQUIRED=1; mkdir -p $(dirname $VALIDATE_RUN_STATE/e9patchcompat/nsswitch.conf) && printf 'aliases: files
automount: files
ethers: files
group: files
gshadow: files
hosts: files
initgroups: files
netgroup: files
netmasks: files
networks: files
passwd: files
protocols: files
publickey: files
rpc: files
services: files
shadow: files
' > $VALIDATE_RUN_STATE/e9patchcompat/nsswitch.conf

steps.desc: e9patch legacy below-L2 stripped verify compatibility: echo
steps.description: One per-program probe of the e9patch-compat-only profile, generated from a row of ci/compat/e9patch. It runs `target/release/hermit --backend e9patch run --strict --epoch=<canonical test epoch> --verify -- <program>` with stdin from /dev/null. That is e9patch binary-rewriting preprocessing with the ptrace backend, not a backend of its own: Hermit rewrites the guest's main ELF with e9tool and e9patch, then runs the rewritten program on the ptrace backend under strict mode, twice, comparing the runs with the Stripped comparator of plain --verify, so no row establishes L2. The rows range from coreutils such as echo and cat to bash pipelines and tests/compat/real_compat_workload.sh workloads; whoami, groups, pinky, logname, tar and chown also bind the files-only nsswitch.conf over /etc/nsswitch.conf. The profile counts every failure as blocking, for example a rewritten binary that crashes or two runs whose output differs.
steps.cmd: "${HERMIT_CORE_TOOLS:?}/with-bound-command" --bindings "${HERMIT_E9PATCH_BINDINGS:?}" --backend e9patch -- bash -c 'export PATH="$PWD/ci/rust-script-bin:$PATH"; export HERMIT_RUST_SCRIPT_ARTIFACT_ROOT="$PWD/target/ci/rust-scripts"; export HERMIT_PREBUILT_RUST_SCRIPTS_REQUIRED=1; mkdir -p $VALIDATE_RUN_STATE/e9patchcompat/compat-tmp/probe-echo $VALIDATE_RUN_STATE/e9patchcompat/compat-tmp/probe-echo/python-cache && export TMPDIR=$VALIDATE_RUN_STATE/e9patchcompat/compat-tmp/probe-echo PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX=$VALIDATE_RUN_STATE/e9patchcompat/compat-tmp/probe-echo/python-cache && "${HERMIT_E9PATCH_BIN:?required measured hermit-e9patch}" run --strict --epoch=2026-01-01T00:00:00Z --verify -- /bin/echo hermit-compat </dev/null'

It runs `target/release/hermit --backend e9patch run --strict --epoch=<canonical test epoch> --verify -- <program>` with stdin from /dev/null. That is e9patch binary-rewriting preprocessing with the ptrace backend, not a backend of its own: Hermit rewrites the guest's main ELF with e9tool and e9patch, then runs the rewritten program on the ptrace backend under strict mode, twice, comparing the runs with the Stripped comparator of plain --verify, so no row establishes L2. The rows range from coreutils such as echo and cat to bash pipelines and tests/compat/real_compat_workload.sh workloads; whoami, groups, pinky, logname, tar and chown also bind the files-only nsswitch.conf over /etc/nsswitch.conf. The profile counts every failure as blocking, for example a rewritten binary that crashes or two runs whose output differs.

It runs `target/release/hermit --backend e9patch run --strict --epoch=<canonical test epoch> --verify -- <program>` with stdin from /dev/null. That is e9patch binary-rewriting preprocessing with the ptrace backend, not a backend of its own: Hermit rewrites the guest's main ELF with e9tool and e9patch, then runs the rewritten program on the ptrace backend under strict mode, twice, comparing the runs with the Stripped comparator of plain --verify, so no row establishes L2. The rows range from coreutils such as echo and cat to bash pipelines and tests/compat/real_compat_workload.sh workloads; whoami, groups, pinky, logname, tar and chown also bind the files-only nsswitch.conf over /etc/nsswitch.conf. The profile counts every failure as blocking, for example a rewritten binary that crashes or two runs whose output differs.
steps.cmd: "${HERMIT_CORE_TOOLS:?}/with-bound-command" --bindings "${HERMIT_E9PATCH_BINDINGS:?}" --backend e9patch -- bash -c 'export PATH="$PWD/ci/rust-script-bin:$PATH"; export HERMIT_RUST_SCRIPT_ARTIFACT_ROOT="$PWD/target/ci/rust-scripts"; export HERMIT_PREBUILT_RUST_SCRIPTS_REQUIRED=1; mkdir -p $VALIDATE_RUN_STATE/e9patchcompat/compat-tmp/probe-mkfifo $VALIDATE_RUN_STATE/e9patchcompat/compat-tmp/probe-mkfifo/python-cache && export TMPDIR=$VALIDATE_RUN_STATE/e9patchcompat/compat-tmp/probe-mkfifo PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX=$VALIDATE_RUN_STATE/e9patchcompat/compat-tmp/probe-mkfifo/python-cache && "${HERMIT_E9PATCH_BIN:?required measured hermit-e9patch}" run --strict --epoch=2026-01-01T00:00:00Z --verify -- bash -c '"'"'set -euo pipefail; p=$(mktemp -u); mkfifo "$p"; stat -c "%F" "$p"; rm -f "$p"'"'"' </dev/null'

steps.desc: SaBRe smoke test (archived backend): ptrace parity and canonical verify of one guest
steps.description: SaBRe is archived (owner, 2026-10-25: no feature work, tests nightly only; ci/manifest-plan/src/archived.rs), so per commit this node is its smoke test, beside the third-party-backends build and Clippy that keep its code compiling. It runs two tests of hermit-cli/tests/sabre_examples.rs, its count pinned by NEXTEST_EXPECTED_EXECUTED, against an explicitly configured SaBRe loader, so a missing loader, libdetcore_sabre.so or revision file fails rather than skips: sabre_root_pid_matches_ptrace requires a root-PID shell probe to give identical status, stdout and stderr under ptrace and --backend sabre, the SaBRe controller's diagnostics to stay out of guest stderr, and the SaBRe run to pass `--verify --verify-strict` with bitwise_parity true; sabre_and_ptrace_detlogs_agree_through_post_exec requires the DETLOG records the SaBRe plugin forwards for /bin/true to equal ptrace's through the post-exec AT_RANDOM record. A SaBRe build that cannot start a guest, leaks a controller line into guest stderr, loses determinism under strict verify or stops forwarding Detcore's records is caught. The suite's other tests (time repeatability, getrandom, forwarding-socket refusals, RDTSC, stack limits, program break, exe links) left the per-commit graph with the archival: run them on demand with the same environment and no -E filter. Until 2026-10-25 this node ran all 36.
steps.cmd: cd -- "${HERMIT_EXTENSION_ROOT:?}" || exit $?; export HERMIT_NEXTEST_PROJECT="$PWD/ci/prepared-project-host.json"; export PATH="${HERMIT_CORE_SOURCE:?}/ci/rust-script-bin:$PATH"; export HERMIT_RUST_SCRIPT_ARTIFACT_ROOT="${HERMIT_CORE_SOURCE:?}/target/ci/rust-scripts"; export HERMIT_PREBUILT_RUST_SCRIPTS_REQUIRED=1; HERMIT_BIN="${HERMIT_CORE_BIN:?}" HERMIT_SABRE_TEST_BINARY="${HERMIT_SABRE_BIN:?}" HERMIT_SABRE_BINARY="${HERMIT_SABRE_LOADER:?}" "${HERMIT_EXTENSION_ROOT:?}/ci/run-owned-nextest.sh" ${CI:+--profile ci} -p hermit-patching-cli --test sabre_examples -j 1 -E 'test(=sabre_root_pid_matches_ptrace) | test(=sabre_and_ptrace_detlogs_agree_through_post_exec)'

steps.desc: Build the separate static patching release frontends
steps.description: Maintained owner of the old host focused compile gate. Separate static frontend package; original 420-wall/2400-CPU/16GiB/8-job bounds retained. Exact selected ELF bindings and published core/cohort identities remain independently required.
steps.cmd: cd -- "${HERMIT_EXTENSION_ROOT:?}" && "${HERMIT_CORE_SOURCE:?}/ci/run-with-core-build.sh" cargo build --release --locked -p hermit-patching-cli --bin hermit-sabre --bin hermit-e9patch

steps.desc: Isolation matrix on ptrace, e9patch and SaBRe, held to its expected-mismatch ledger
steps.description: Runs the backend isolation matrix (tests/isolation/conformance.rs, the container contract of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4009) for every required cell of ptrace, e9patch preprocessing with ptrace and SaBRe (the backends on ptrace's runtime); measured 218 s serially in the pinned root: the probe tests/isolation/backend_isolation.c beside a native baseline, each command a bounded child of the local executor, up to HERMIT_ISOLATION_JOBS cells at once (the cells of one cohort, which share an input fixture across backends, one at a time; output and the ledger check keep the selection order), every assertion row checked by hermit-cli/tests/common/backend_isolation.rs. No cell fully matches on any backend yet, so the node holds the matrix to tests/isolation/expected-mismatches.tsv: every cell that collects no guest observations, and every assertion that does not match, must be a ledger row naming its backend and linking its issue, and a row that no longer describes a failure on a backend it names fails the node until it is deleted, so what now matches stays matched. The ledger was measured in this pinned root; two host runs agreed cell for cell. Artifacts (assertion rows, per-backend totals, the required-cell ledger) are kept in target/ci/isolation-matrix/ptrace-runtime. It publishes one structured result row per cell it checks, through ci/conformance-test-counts.sh, so validate's per-node coverage counts it as executed; until 2026-10-17 it wrote none, and every full validation that planned it was NOT-VALIDATED. The complete original ptrace/e9patch/SaBRe matrix stays one strict aggregate under the patching physical catalog, reusing the neutral common core driver with exact measured static frontend bindings; native baselines, shared input cohorts, complete mismatch/staleness ledger and all original resource limits are unchanged.

then printf -v hermit_extra '"'"' %q'"'"' "$@"; hermit_payload+=$hermit_extra; fi && exec bash -c "$hermit_payload"' bash 'export PATH="$PWD/ci/rust-script-bin:$PATH"; export HERMIT_RUST_SCRIPT_ARTIFACT_ROOT="$PWD/target/ci/rust-scripts"; export HERMIT_PREBUILT_RUST_SCRIPTS_REQUIRED=1; rm -rf target/ci/isolation-matrix/ptrace-runtime && mkdir -p target/ci/isolation-matrix && "${HERMIT_CORE_SOURCE:?}/ci/conformance-test-counts.sh" target/ci/isolation-matrix/ptrace-runtime -- "${HERMIT_CORE_SOURCE:?}/tests/isolation/conformance.rs" --hermit "${HERMIT_CORE_BIN:?}" --command-bindings "${HERMIT_E2E_COMMAND_BINDINGS:?}" --executor local --expected tests/isolation/expected-mismatches.tsv --jobs "${HERMIT_ISOLATION_JOBS:-1}" --backends ptrace,e9patch,sabre --artifacts target/ci/isolation-matrix/ptrace-runtime'
